title: Failure
hook: Peter failed and was trusted again
tomorrow: Thomas wouldn't believe without touching. was that so wrong?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the manna that wouldn't keep: one day at a time, with help, and the bread came again after a slip. Today, the slip everyone saw.
screen: `ONE DAY AT A TIME.` → `THE SLIP EVERYONE SAW.`

segments.voice: A missed penalty gets replayed forever. Peter's worst night does too. He swore he'd die before he'd deny Jesus, and hours later he's warming his hands at a fire of coals in the high priest's courtyard, telling a servant girl he doesn't know the man. Then comes the strange part. At the very end of John's Gospel, after the resurrection, there's another fire of coals, on a beach, with Jesus cooking breakfast. Why would John light the same fire twice?
screen: `REPLAYED FOREVER.` → `A FIRE OF COALS, AND A DENIAL.` → `THE SAME FIRE, TWICE?`

segments.voice: Peter and the others have fished all night and caught nothing. A man on the shore tells them where to cast, the net fills, and Peter jumps into the sea. On land, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "they saw hot coals lying, and a fish laid thereon, and bread." After they eat, Jesus asks Peter a question. Simon, son of John, lovest thou me? Then he asks again. Then a third time, and Peter is grieved: "Lord, thou knowest all things: thou knowest that I love thee." Here's the puzzle solved, the way many readers hear it. Three denials by one fire; three questions by another. Jesus doesn't pretend the courtyard never happened. He brings Peter back to the smell of the same kind of smoke and lets him say yes as many times as he said no. Then he gives him a job: "Feed my sheep." The man who failed loudest isn't benched. He's handed the flock. Here's one for a friend tonight: John records no scolding for the denial. Just a fire, breakfast, and three questions. Catholics carry that pattern into confession: name the failure plainly, hear it forgiven, and walk out with work still to do. Failure in this story isn't where the trust ends. It's where it starts again.
screen: `HOT COALS, A FISH, AND BREAD.` · `LOVEST THOU ME? THREE TIMES.` · `THE SAME SMOKE, A NEW YES.` · `FEED MY SHEEP.` · then, large: `TRUSTED AGAIN.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, write one failure you still replay, just a few words. Under it, write two more: trusted again. If you pray, you can hold the paper and say Peter's line, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee; if not, let the second line sit under the first for the rest of the sit.
Failure. Falling short of what you swore you'd do. In Peter's story, it's the place the trust starts over.
Hold onto this: trusted again, because Peter got the flock after the fire, not before. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1710 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THOMAS WOULDN'T BELIEVE WITHOUT TOUCHING. WAS THAT SO WRONG?`

howItsDone: Catholics bring their failures to the sacrament of confession, naming them to a priest, hearing the words of absolution and receiving a small penance; John 21 is read at Mass in the Easter season.

fork.setup: your teammate missed the deciding penalty last season. now it's a shootout again, and she asks to take one. by John 21's pattern, what does the coach do?
options: talk it through with her, then hand her the ball.
bench her until she proves herself in practice.
hand her the ball and never mention the miss.
fork.reveal: Jesus doesn't skip the failure (three questions by a fire) and doesn't bench Peter: feed my sheep. trusted again.

original.note: Greek, John 18:18 and 21:9: a charcoal fire, the word John uses for both fires.

what a scholar hears: the charcoal fire (anthrakia) of John 18:18 returning in John 21:9, and the threefold question of John 21:15–17 answering the threefold denial.

chat.says: i said "he'll just relapse again" about Nico. Val heard. how do i come back from that?
options: Own it to Val straight, then keep showing up. Peter failed loud and was trusted again.
Give it time and don't bring it up. Mentioning it just reopens the whole thing.
You probably can't. Some failures are too big, and she won't trust you the same.
chat.meaning: Peter denied Jesus, then was met at a fire, asked to say his love again, and handed the flock. A failure can be where trust starts again.
